newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures stabilise after Thursday's falls.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures stabilise after Thursday's falls.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures steadied on Friday after Thursday's fall in prices which followed news that Germany planned to sell $230 million worth of oil from its reserves.

August Brent was two cents firmer at 1016 GMT, and stood at $17.98, after trading in thin volumes in a narrow eight-cent range. August gas oil, the new front month, had gained 25 cents a tonne to stand at $162.
"The market is unchanged," one broker said. "There is nothing new out there - nobody is taking a view."

A German government source said on Friday that about 2.8 million barrels of oil would be sold in the next few weeks as the first tranche in the sale of the government's entire 7.3 million tonne reserve by the end of 1999.
"While the sale is not of a huge amount, it is the trend that is disturbing," brokers GNI said in a daily report.
The oil sale announcement came against a background of the prospect of renewed Iraqi barrels coming onto world markets under the country's $2 billion oil-for-food deal with the U.N.
Iraqi and U.N. officials are due to meet on Sunday to talk about an aid distribution plan which Baghdad wants finalised before it resumes exports.

MeesPierson Derivatives in London, employing the Market Profile technique, said: "Preparation is now negative, so lower prices are expected. They pegged support at $17.85, $17.70 and $17.64, while resistance levels lay at $18.03, $18.15 and $18.33.
Others pointed to important support at $17.50, roughly the lowest point reached on the August Brent contract chart on June 20. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
